To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a hierarchical Markov chain to model IEEE 802.1 DCF networks, we solved the Markov chain, we obtained analytical expressions for the QoS metrics of DCF and we compared them with simulation results.

we propose a hierarchical three-dimensional (3D) Markov chain model that is able to fully capture, for non-saturated IEEE802.11 DFC networks, the Quality of Service performance metrics and the queueing behavior, which is not possible with two-dimensional Markov chain models.
we propose a hierarchical three-dimensional mean-field Markov chain to model the QoS performance of a non-saturated IEEE802.11 DFC-based wireless network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of IEEE 802.15.4 networks.
the analysis of IEEE 802.15.1 networks, and in particular with the modeling and performance evaluation of the MAC layer.
the development of analytical techniques for the performance analysis of wireless LANs based on the IEEE 802.1 1 MAC protocol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is the most accurate and general model for the IEEE 802. 11 DCF to date.
the proposed model provides an accurate analytical framework to evaluate the performance of DCF-based IEEE802.11 networks under realistic non-saturated traffic and error-prone conditions.

the 3D model presented here can be used to predict the impact of buffer sizes, block error probabilities and freezing rules on the performance of non-saturated networks with a high degree of accuracy, while keeping the computational complexity at a manageable level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in this paper, we propose a new analytical model for non-saturated IEEE802.11 networks, which is able to capture the impact of buffer length, error probability and freezing rules on all QoS performance metrics.
, for the first time, a Markov chain model is able to provide accurate analytical results for a wide range of QoS performance parameters in non-saturated IEEE802.11 networks.
we have developed a hierarchical three-dimensional model to analyze IEEE 802. 11 DCF networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed hierarchical three-dimensional Markow chain can be used to accurately predict the performance of IEEE 802.1 networks in terms of delay, packet drop rate and throughput.

the proposed hierarchical three-dimensional Markove model is able to capture, in a computationally efficient manner, the QoS performance of IEEE 802. 11 DCF-based network under a wide variety of traffic load and channel error conditions.
the proposed model is a powerful tool for the performance analysis of IEEE 802. 11 networks under non-saturated traffic conditions and error-prone channel assumptions.
